sentences.text: Case diary is perused.

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023, seeking grant of regular bail in connection with Crime No.19 of 2021 registered at Police Station Kotwali,
District Bhind (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 409, 420, 406, 34 of IPC.

According to the prosecution case, the complainant Mahesh Singh Chauhan submitted an application at Kotwali police station on 08.01.2021 to the effect that on 22.04.2015, his nephew Chetan Chauhan (son of his younger brother Subhash) since was getting married, for the purpose of making jewelry for the wedding, on 11.04.2015, 340 grams of gold was given to the accused.
Additionally, an amount of Rs.5,00,000 was deposited separately in relation to 171 grams of gold.
The accused had assured that he would make the jewelry, but neither did he deliver the jewelry nor did he NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17217 2 MCRC-25344-2025 return the gold or money
. A case was registered in this regard and, during the course of investigation, the accused was arrested.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The transaction, if any, is purely of a civil nature, but it has been given a criminal color.

sentences.text: The alleged incident dates back to the year 2015, and the FIR was lodged after a substantial delay in 2021, raising serious doubts about its authenticity.

It is further submitted that the witness Dinesh Singh Chauhan in another case, in his cross-examination dated 22.01.2018 in paragraph 6 had clearly stated that he had no monetary dealings with Ramsevak, Rishi (present applicant), or Bhagwat Dayal and when the complainant Mahesh Singh Chauhan himself, in his statement before the court, did not make any direct allegation of financial transaction or criminal breach of trust against the present applicant this F.I.R. alleging criminal breach of trust is frivolous.
However, in the registered FIR, the alleged incident is shown to have continued from 2015 to 2021.
This contradiction raises serious doubts about the veracity of the prosecution's case.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent and undertakes to cooperate in the trial.
He is in jail since 28.05.2024.

Hence,
in light of the aforesaid circumstances, the applicant prays to be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out.

Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17217 3 MCRC-25344-2025 available on record.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the fact that complainant Dinesh Singh Chauhan, in his cross- examination dated 22.01.2018 (paragraph no. 6) in another case had clearly stated that he had no monetary dealings with Ramsevak, Rishi (present applicant),
or Bhagwat Dayal and did not make any direct allegations of financial transaction or criminal breach of trust against the present applicant, the credibility of the prosecution's case becomes doubtful.
Additionally, there is considerable delay in lodging the FIR (incident alleged to have occurred in 2015, FIR lodged in 2021).
In view of the above facts and circumstances, this Court finds it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 CrPC is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
